webhook_broker_pillar.meta_title: TradingView Webhook to Broker: How It Works | PickMyTrade
webhook_broker_pillar.meta_description: How a TradingView (or TrendSpider) alert becomes a live broker order: the webhook pipeline, payload flow, latency budget, security model, and every broker PickMyTrade connects to.
webhook_broker_pillar.hero_subtitle: A plain-English walkthrough of the webhook-to-broker bridge: how PickMyTrade turns a TradingView or TrendSpider alert into an executed order at your broker or prop-firm account — no coding required.
webhook_broker_pillar.what_p1: A webhook is just an HTTP message one system sends to another the moment something happens. In trading automation, TradingView (or TrendSpider) fires that message the instant your alert condition is met, and PickMyTrade is the service on the receiving end that turns it into a real order.
webhook_broker_pillar.what_p2: PickMyTrade itself is not a broker, not a prop firm, and not a signal provider — it never holds your funds or generates trade ideas. It is the automation layer in between: it authenticates the incoming webhook, applies the order rules you configured, and calls your connected broker's or prop firm's own API to place the trade on the account they hold.
webhook_broker_pillar.what_note: Because the bridge is stateless and cloud-hosted, it runs 24/7 — your alert still fires even if your charting laptop is asleep or your browser tab is closed.
webhook_broker_pillar.pipeline_subtitle: The same six steps run for every supported broker and prop firm — only the final API call changes.
webhook_broker_pillar.step1_desc: Define your entry/exit condition on a chart or strategy exactly as you normally would — no special syntax needed at this stage.
webhook_broker_pillar.step2_desc: Click "Generate Alert" in your PickMyTrade dashboard. It auto-writes the JSON alert message and gives you a unique, private webhook URL — zero coding.
webhook_broker_pillar.step3_desc: Drop the JSON into the alert's message box and the webhook URL into TradingView's webhook field, then save. Setup takes about five minutes.
webhook_broker_pillar.step4_desc: When your condition triggers, TradingView POSTs the JSON payload to PickMyTrade's cloud endpoint, live 24/7, independent of your own computer.
webhook_broker_pillar.step5_desc: The payload is parsed and matched against your configured instrument mapping, position size, bracket take-profit/stop-loss, and any risk limits before an order is built.
webhook_broker_pillar.step6_desc: PickMyTrade calls your specific broker's or prop firm's API to place the order, and the fill confirmation flows back to your dashboard — typically in under 200ms end to end.
webhook_broker_pillar.latency_p1: Every extra millisecond between your alert firing and your order reaching the exchange is a millisecond the market can move against you. PickMyTrade's cloud infrastructure targets sub-200ms webhook-to-order routing on typical setups, so fast-moving futures and forex signals get filled close to the price that triggered them.
webhook_broker_pillar.latency_p2: Running in the cloud instead of on a local script also removes the most common failure point in DIY webhook setups: a laptop that goes to sleep, a Wi-Fi drop, or a closed browser tab. PickMyTrade listens for your webhook continuously, so the same alert behaves the same way at 3pm or 3am.
webhook_broker_pillar.security_p1: Your webhook URL is unique to your account and acts as its own credential — treat it like a password and never post it publicly, since anyone with the URL could send it orders.
webhook_broker_pillar.security_p2: As a second guardrail, PickMyTrade lets you cap position size, set daily loss limits, and attach automatic take-profit/stop-loss brackets to every routed order, so a misfiring strategy can't exceed the boundaries you set — including the specific drawdown and daily-loss rules required by prop firms.
webhook_broker_pillar.security_p3: PickMyTrade never custodies funds. Every order it routes executes on the account you already hold directly with your broker or prop firm; PickMyTrade only has the trading permissions you grant when connecting that account.
webhook_broker_pillar.brokers_subtitle: The pipeline above is identical across all 12+ supported brokers, prop-firm platforms, and exchanges — pick your connection and follow its dedicated guide.
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_q1: What exactly is a "webhook" in TradingView automation?
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_a1: It's an outbound HTTP request TradingView sends the moment your alert condition is met. Instead of just popping up a notification, TradingView posts the alert's JSON message to a URL you provide — in this case, PickMyTrade's endpoint — which is what lets an alert trigger a real trade instead of just a phone buzz.
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_q2: Do I need to know how to code to set this up?
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_a2: No. PickMyTrade auto-generates the JSON payload and webhook URL for you from a simple dashboard form. You copy both into TradingView's alert dialog — no scripting, no API keys to hand-write.
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_a3: PickMyTrade targets sub-200ms from the moment it receives your webhook to the moment the order reaches your broker or prop-firm account on typical setups. Actual fill speed also depends on your broker's own matching engine and market conditions.
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_a4: Each webhook URL is unique to your account and functions as its authentication token. Keep it private the same way you would an API key — anyone who has it can send your account orders.
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_q5: Can one TradingView alert route to multiple brokers or accounts?
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_a5: Yes. You can connect multiple broker and prop-firm accounts in PickMyTrade and configure a strategy to fan an alert out to several of them at once, each with its own position size and risk settings.
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_q6: What happens if my computer or TradingView tab is closed?
webhook_broker_pillar.faq_a6: Nothing changes on PickMyTrade's side — it's a cloud service that listens for your webhook 24/7. As long as TradingView's own alert (which runs server-side once created) fires, PickMyTrade receives and routes it regardless of whether your local device is on.

broker_ib.faq_subtitle: Everything you need to know about TradingView to Interactive Brokers automation
broker_ib.faq1_q: Can you automate TradingView alerts to Interactive Brokers?
broker_ib.faq1_a: Yes. PickMyTrade connects TradingView to Interactive Brokers, so when your TradingView alert fires, PickMyTrade places the matching order on your IBKR account through TWS or IB Gateway. There is no coding involved. You paste a PickMyTrade webhook URL and alert message into a TradingView alert, and PickMyTrade handles execution on IBKR for stocks, options and futures.
broker_ib.faq2_q: How do I connect TradingView to Interactive Brokers without coding?
broker_ib.faq2_a: Install and log in to TWS or IB Gateway, turn on API access in the settings, then connect that account inside PickMyTrade. Generate your webhook URL and alert message in PickMyTrade and paste them into a TradingView alert. When the alert triggers, PickMyTrade routes the order to IBKR. You never touch the IB API directly and you do not write any code.
broker_ib.faq5_q: What can I trade on IBKR through PickMyTrade (stocks, options, futures)?
broker_ib.faq5_a: You can trade the main IBKR asset classes: stocks and ETFs, options, and futures, across the exchanges your IBKR account is permitted to access. Because Interactive Brokers is a global multi-asset broker, this covers far more than futures alone, which is the main reason traders pick IBKR for automation. It works on both paper and live accounts.
broker_ib.faq6_q: Does PickMyTrade store my Interactive Brokers login or API credentials?
broker_ib.faq6_a: No. PickMyTrade connects through the Interactive Brokers API using TWS or IB Gateway, which you log in to yourself. Your IBKR username and password stay with Interactive Brokers, and you authorize the API connection inside your own TWS or Gateway. PickMyTrade sends orders over that authorized connection rather than storing your broker login.
broker_ib.faq7_q: How fast are orders executed and is this suitable for scalping?
broker_ib.faq7_a: PickMyTrade processes your order in under 200ms on our side. Total time from chart to fill also depends on TradingView's webhook delivery, the round trip to IBKR through TWS or IB Gateway, and IBKR's own routing. This suits swing and intraday strategies well. It is not designed for sub-minute high-frequency scalping where microseconds decide the outcome.

broker_ib.faq9_a_pre: Yes. PickMyTrade can route a single TradingView alert to one or more Interactive Brokers accounts, so you can mirror the same strategy across several accounts. You map each alert to the account or accounts you want it to trade. See the

broker_matchtrader.webhook_step1_text: Create a PickMyTrade account, then add your Match-Trader broker account with your broker login. Set your default risk settings, such as position size, stop-loss and take-profit, inside PickMyTrade.
broker_matchtrader.webhook_step2_lead: Generate your webhook URL and alert message.
broker_matchtrader.webhook_step2_text: PickMyTrade creates the webhook URL and a ready-made JSON payload that carries the entries and exits your own strategy defines. You never build any JSON by hand.
broker_matchtrader.webhook_step3_text: On your strategy or indicator, open Create Alert, clear the default message, and paste the PickMyTrade alert message. Under Notifications, switch on Webhook URL and paste the PickMyTrade webhook URL. Webhook alerts require a paid TradingView plan (Pro, Pro+ or Premium), because free TradingView accounts cannot send webhooks.

broker_projectx.explained_heading: Is ProjectX the same as TopstepX? What changed in 2026
broker_projectx.explained_p1: ProjectX was a futures trading engine that powered many prop firms' platforms. In late 2025 ProjectX announced it was winding down its third-party service, and on 28 February 2026 it ended licensing to outside prop firms. The technology did not disappear. Topstep took it exclusive and rebranded it as TopstepX, the platform Topstep now uses for its evaluations, funded accounts, and live brokerage product.
broker_projectx.explained_p2: What this means in practice: if you used ProjectX through another firm before 2026, that firm has since moved to a different engine. Today, when people say "ProjectX," they are almost always trading on TopstepX. The two names point to the same underlying technology, and PickMyTrade connects to it the same way either way, using a TopstepX API key.

trade_copier.hero_subtitle: PickMyTrade is a cloud trade copier that mirrors your trades across futures and prop firm accounts in real time. Copy from a master broker account, or automate straight from a TradingView alert or strategy, and every connected account fills the matching order at once. trade_copier.s2_p1: A trade copier is software that takes one trade and replicates it across other trading accounts automatically. One account acts as the leader, often called the master or the source, and the others follow it. The moment the leader enters, exits, or adjusts a position, the trade copier software places the same order on every follower account in real time. People also call this a trade replicator, a trade duplicator, or an order replicator, and the wider category gets labeled copy trading software, a copy trading tool, a copy trading platform, or link trading software. The idea never changes: make one decision once, then let the tool replicate it everywhere instead of repeating the same clicks account by account.
trade_copier.s2_p2: Traders reach for a trade copier for two reasons. The first is scale. If you run several prop firm evaluations, a couple of funded accounts and a personal account, placing each order by hand is slow and error-prone, and a half-second of hesitation on the fifth account can mean a worse fill or a missed trade entirely. The second is consistency. A copier keeps every account on the same plan, with the same entries, exits, stop-loss and take-profit, so your results do not drift apart because you fat-fingered a size somewhere.
trade_copier.s2_p3: As a retail trade copier, PickMyTrade is built for individual traders rather than fund managers routing client money. It copies your own signals across your own connected accounts, and it does that in the cloud, so there is no server for you to babysit. The rest of this page explains exactly how it works, which brokers and prop firms it fits, how per-account sizing works, and how a cloud copier compares with the older local and VPS tools.
trade_copier.s3_intro: PickMyTrade is a TradingView automation platform first and a copier second, so you get two ways to feed it, both running in the cloud.
trade_copier.s3_mode1_title: Automate from a TradingView alert or strategy
trade_copier.s3_mode1_desc: This is the path most traders use. When your TradingView strategy, indicator or manual chart alert fires, TradingView sends a small webhook message to PickMyTrade, which reads the symbol, side, size and risk settings, then places the matching order on every account you have connected. One alert reaches many accounts at once, across all supported brokers. Webhook alerts need a paid TradingView plan (Pro, Pro+ or Premium), because free TradingView accounts cannot send webhooks.
trade_copier.s3_mode2_title: Copy from a master broker account
trade_copier.s3_mode2_desc: Prefer to trade by hand? On Tradovate, PickMyTrade includes a Manual Trade Copier: place a trade on your admin (master) account and it mirrors out to your client (sub) accounts in real time. Sub-accounts under the same login are covered by one subscription, and external accounts on a different login are added with their own PickMyTrade token. Every copied trade is tracked with a master and slave order ID, and a stop button halts copying instantly. This master-account mirroring is a Tradovate feature; for other brokers, use the TradingView alert path.
trade_copier.s3_cloud_title: Cloud-based, no VPS, no desktop install
trade_copier.s3_cloud_desc: The whole copier runs on hosted servers, 24/7. There is no download-and-run program on your laptop and no virtual private server to rent and keep online. Once your accounts are connected and your alert is live, trades keep copying even when your computer and your broker's app are switched off. That is the big practical difference from the older generation of local copiers, and it is why a cloud copier fits traders who are not at a desk all day.
trade_copier.s3_realtime_title: Real-time order and position mirroring, with per-account sizing
trade_copier.s3_realtime_desc: Whichever path you use, entries, exits, stop-loss and take-profit copy to every connected account, and the take-profit and stop-loss prices stay identical across accounts. What is not identical, on purpose, is size. Every account carries its own quantity multiplier, so a single signal can trade one contract on a small evaluation and several on a larger funded account. That combination, identical prices with per-account sizing, is what makes this a real trade replication engine rather than a blunt one-size-fits-all copier.
trade_copier.s4_intro: PickMyTrade copies and automates across ten brokers. TradingView is the signal source on every path; the master-account Manual Trade Copier is a Tradovate feature.
trade_copier.s4_note: Not supported, so you know before you sign up: PickMyTrade does not copy or automate MT4, MT5, NinjaTrader, DXtrade or OANDA, and it does not read signals from Telegram. cTrader is live now. If your broker is not on the list above, PickMyTrade is not the right tool for that account, and we would rather tell you that up front.
trade_copier.s5_h2: Copy trades across prop firm accounts
trade_copier.s5_p1: The biggest reason traders want a copier is prop firms. If you run several evaluations or funded accounts, routing one signal across all of them is how you scale without watching every account by hand. PickMyTrade connects to accounts on Tradovate, Rithmic and ProjectX, which many prop firms run on, so you can route your own TradingView alerts across your own funded and evaluation accounts. Firms that commonly run on those platforms include Apex Trader Funding, Topstep, Alpha Futures, Take Profit Trader, FundedNext Futures, MyFundedFutures, TradeDay and Tradeify.
trade_copier.s5_p2: Here is the honest part most tool pages skip. Copy trading and automation rules vary by prop firm and change over time. Some firms allow copying your own alerts across the funded accounts you own, and treat that very differently from external copy trading, such as subscribing to a third-party signal seller or letting someone else manage your funded account. PickMyTrade is built for the first case: it copies your own signals across your own accounts, so you stay in control. We do not label any firm as copy-friendly, and we do not claim that a specific firm allows automation, because those policies change over time. Always confirm your firm's current policy before you go live.

trade_copier.s6_intro: The TradingView path, from zero to copying across every account, in five real steps. Most traders finish in well under an hour.
trade_copier.s6_step1_desc: Create a PickMyTrade account and connect each broker account you want to copy to, whether live, demo or a prop-firm evaluation. Add as many accounts under the same login as you like.
trade_copier.s6_step2_title: Set your source and per-account multipliers
trade_copier.s6_step2_desc: Pick your source of trades, then set a quantity multiplier for each account so every account trades the size you want (0.5x, 1x, 2x and so on). You can also switch copying on or off per account.
trade_copier.s6_step3_title: Generate the alert message and webhook URL
trade_copier.s6_step3_desc: Inside PickMyTrade, generate the alert message and the webhook URL for your buy and sell signals. There is nothing to code; the platform builds the message for you.
trade_copier.s6_step4_title: Paste them into a TradingView alert
trade_copier.s6_step4_desc: Create an alert on your strategy or indicator, delete the default text, paste the PickMyTrade message, then set the webhook URL in the alert's notifications tab. Webhooks need a paid TradingView plan (Pro, Pro+ or Premium).
trade_copier.s6_step5_title: Test on a 1-minute chart, then go live
trade_copier.s6_step5_desc: Fire a test alert, check your PickMyTrade alert log and confirm the fills in your broker, then enable the alert. From now on, one signal copies across all connected accounts automatically. Trading Tradovate by hand instead? Use the Manual Trade Copier and place trades on your master account.
trade_copier.s7_p1: The real power of an automated trade copier is that not every account should trade the same size. Every account gets its own quantity multiplier, and the math is simple: client position equals master position times the multiplier. So a 2-contract signal becomes 1 contract on a 0.5x account, 2 on a 1x account, 4 on a 2x account and 6 on a 3x account. Decimal multipliers like 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 are supported, and the final quantity rounds to a whole number. That lets you run a small evaluation at 0.5x, a mid-size funded account at 1x and a larger account at 2x, all from the same signal, while each account stays inside its own risk limit.
trade_copier.s7_p2: On the TradingView webhook path you also get proper risk tooling, not just sizing. You can copy Market, Limit and Stop orders, attach stop-loss and take-profit with five methods (points or dollar value, percentage, price levels, ticks, or total profit and loss), add a trailing stop, reverse or flip a position, meaning close the current position and open the opposite one, or scale into an existing position on a same-direction signal. Position size can be a fixed quantity or a risk percentage, so the copier fits both aggressive scaling and careful risk-first sizing.
trade_copier.s7_p3: You also stay in control at the account level. Turn copying on or off for any account, so a signal only reaches the accounts you want it to, and use the stop control to halt copying instantly if you need to step in. One note on scope: the reverse and flip and scale-in behaviors, the trailing stop and the five stop-loss and take-profit methods live on the TradingView webhook path. The Tradovate Manual Trade Copier supports Market, Limit, Stop, Stop-Limit and bracket orders on market entries, so choose the path that matches how you trade.
trade_copier.s8_h2: Cloud vs local and VPS trade copiers
trade_copier.s8_p1: There are two broad kinds of trade copier, and it is worth being straight about the tradeoffs. A local or VPS copier runs as a program on a machine you keep online, often on a rented virtual private server so it does not stop when your laptop sleeps. Native desktop copiers that talk directly to a broker's API can be faster on raw latency, because there is no cloud hop between the signal and the order. If you are a pure speed scalper chasing every last millisecond, a well-tuned local copier next to your broker can win on that single metric.
trade_copier.s8_p2: A cloud trade copier like PickMyTrade makes a different trade. There is nothing to install, no VPS to rent and configure, no updates to babysit, and it keeps copying when your computer is off. PickMyTrade processes your order in under 200ms on our side; total fill time also depends on your broker's execution, network latency, and how quickly TradingView sends the alert, so we do not promise a guaranteed end-to-end fill speed. What we do promise is reach and convenience: one platform copies across ten brokers and many accounts, from any device, on a flat price.
trade_copier.s8_p3: For most multi-account and prop firm traders, that is the right trade. You are not shaving microseconds off a single fill; you are trying to get one strategy onto five, ten or twenty accounts reliably, without renting servers or leaving a desktop running. That is where a cloud copier is hard to beat, and it is why PickMyTrade wins on no-install setup, mobile access, broker breadth and a flat monthly cost rather than on raw latency.
trade_copier.s9_p1: Because the copying happens in the cloud and you manage it through the browser, PickMyTrade is operating-system agnostic. It works as a Windows trade copier, a macOS trade copier and a mobile trade copier from the same account, with nothing to download on any of them. There is no Windows-only executable and no separate Mac build to keep updated, which is a common headache with older download-and-run copiers that only ship for one platform.
trade_copier.s9_p2: Set it up on a desktop, then check your alert log and toggle accounts from your phone on the go. The trades themselves keep copying whether your device is a laptop, a desktop or a tablet, and whether it is on or off, because the engine lives on our servers rather than on your machine. For traders who split time between a home desk and a phone, that OS-agnostic, always-on design is the whole point of moving the copier to the cloud.

Every account starts with a 7-day free trial, and no credit card is required, so you can test copy trading before you pay a cent. broker_tradelocker.new_steps_title: How do I connect TradeLocker to TradingView step by step?
broker_tradelocker.new_steps_intro: The full setup takes about five minutes and there is nothing to code. Here are the four steps.
broker_tradelocker.new_steps_1_title: Step 1: Create your PickMyTrade account and get your webhook URL
broker_tradelocker.new_steps_1_text: Sign up for PickMyTrade and start your 7-day free trial (no credit card needed). Inside the dashboard, generate your alert and PickMyTrade gives you a unique webhook URL. This URL is the address TradingView will send your signals to, so keep it handy for step 3.
broker_tradelocker.new_steps_2_title: Step 2: Add your TradeLocker credentials (email, password, server/environment, demo vs live)
broker_tradelocker.new_steps_2_text: Open the TradeLocker connection screen in PickMyTrade and enter the login you use for TradeLocker: your email, your password, and your server or broker environment. Choose whether the account is demo or live. Because TradeLocker is offered through many different brokers, the server value tells PickMyTrade which broker environment your account lives on. Save the connection and PickMyTrade links to your TradeLocker account.
broker_tradelocker.new_steps_3_title: Step 3: Build the TradingView alert with the PMT JSON message (entry, SL, TP, quantity)
broker_tradelocker.new_steps_3_text: In PickMyTrade, generate the alert message for your buy and sell signals. It is a small JSON block that carries the symbol, order side, quantity, and any stop-loss or take-profit you want. In TradingView, create an alert on your strategy or indicator, delete the default alert text, and paste the PickMyTrade message into the message box. Then open the alert's Notifications tab and paste your PickMyTrade webhook URL into the Webhook URL field. Webhook alerts require a paid TradingView plan (Pro, Pro+, or Premium); free TradingView accounts cannot send webhooks.
broker_tradelocker.new_steps_4_title: Step 4: Fire a test alert and confirm the order in TradeLocker
broker_tradelocker.new_steps_4_text: Before you trust it with a live strategy, send one test alert. Put the alert on a fast timeframe or trigger it manually, then check the PickMyTrade alert log to see the signal arrive, and check TradeLocker to confirm the order landed. Once you see the trade appear in TradeLocker, your connection is working and you can enable your real strategy.
broker_tradelocker.new_vs_title: How does PickMyTrade compare with other TradingView-to-TradeLocker tools?

PickMyTrade runs entirely in the cloud, so there is no VPS to rent and no desktop app to keep open, and it handles both single-account automation and multi-account copying in one subscription. It processes your order in under 200ms on our side, supports symbol mapping, multipliers, and risk-percentage sizing, and connects to many brokers beyond TradeLocker if you expand later. Whichever tool you pick, test it on a demo account first and confirm it fits your prop firm's rules.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_subtitle: Answers written to match our TradingView-to-TradeLocker how-to guide above
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q1_q: Can you connect TradingView to TradeLocker?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q1_a: Yes. TradingView cannot place orders in TradeLocker on its own, but PickMyTrade connects the two using webhook alerts. When your TradingView alert fires, PickMyTrade receives it and places the matching order in your TradeLocker account automatically, with no coding and no computer left running. Most traders are live in about five minutes.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q2_q: How do I connect TradeLocker to PickMyTrade / TradingView?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q2_a: Create a PickMyTrade account, open the TradeLocker connection screen and enter your TradeLocker email, password, and server or broker environment, choosing demo or live. Then generate your alert message and webhook URL in PickMyTrade, create an alert in TradingView, paste the message into the alert box and the webhook URL into the alert's Notifications tab. Fire a test alert to confirm it works.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q3_q: What credentials and information does TradeLocker require to connect?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q3_a: PickMyTrade needs the same details you use to log in to TradeLocker: your email, your password, and your server or broker environment name. You also tell PickMyTrade whether the account is a demo or a live account. Because TradeLocker is offered through many brokers, the server value is what points PickMyTrade at the correct broker environment.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q4_q: Where do I find my TradeLocker server name / broker environment?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q4_a: Your server or environment name appears on the TradeLocker login screen, next to the email and password fields, on both the web and mobile apps. It is set by the broker that gave you the TradeLocker account. If you are not sure which one to use, open your broker's TradeLocker login page and copy the server value exactly as shown, or ask your broker's support which environment your account uses.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q5_q: Do I need to know how to code to automate TradingView to TradeLocker?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q5_a: No. PickMyTrade is a no-code tool. It generates the alert message and webhook URL for you, and all you do is paste them into a TradingView alert. There is nothing to program, no API keys to write, and no plugin to install.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q6_q: Can I copy one TradingView signal to multiple TradeLocker accounts?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q6_a: Yes. PickMyTrade works as a TradeLocker trade copier, so a single TradingView alert can place the same trade across several TradeLocker accounts at once. Each account can have its own quantity multiplier (for example 0.5x, 1x and 2x from the same alert) or use risk-percentage sizing, so you can scale size up or down per account while keeping the same entry, stop-loss, and take-profit.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q7_q: Can I test on a TradeLocker demo account before going live?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q7_a: Yes. When you add your TradeLocker credentials you choose demo or live, so you can connect a demo account and run your whole setup on paper first. Testing on demo is the safest way to confirm your alerts, symbol mapping, and sizing behave the way you expect before you risk real money.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q8_q: What order types, stop loss and take profit options are supported?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q8_a: On the webhook path PickMyTrade supports market and limit orders and lets you attach a stop-loss and a take-profit to the entry. You can also reverse or flip a position and send a close-all command. If your TradingView strategy manages its own exits, including multiple take-profits such as TP1 and TP2, let the strategy handle them and do not add extra stop-loss or take-profit settings in PickMyTrade; if it does not, set them once in PickMyTrade and every alert follows them.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q9_q: Can I trade a different symbol than the one in my alert (symbol mapping)?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q9_a: Yes. PickMyTrade includes symbol mapping, so the symbol in your TradingView alert can be different from the symbol executed in TradeLocker. This is useful when your chart symbol and your broker's instrument name do not match exactly, and it lets you point one alert at the correct TradeLocker instrument. You can enter the symbol to trade directly in PickMyTrade; it is mandatory for stop-loss types such as Ticks or Total Profit/Loss, and if you leave it blank PickMyTrade uses the symbol from your TradingView chart.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q10_q: Why did my trade fail to place / get rejected, and how do I fix it?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q10_a: The most common causes are a symbol that does not match a symbol your broker lists, a position size larger than your account or broker allows, a closed market, or not enough margin. Connection issues are usually a wrong password or a server or environment value that does not match your TradeLocker login. Open the PickMyTrade alert log to see exactly what arrived and what the broker returned; that tells you whether the fix is in the TradingView alert, the PickMyTrade settings, or your broker account. If a trade never appears at all, confirm your TradingView plan is Pro or higher (free plans cannot send webhooks), that the webhook URL and the alert message are pasted into the right fields, that your TradeLocker connection is active, and that your strategy is actually generating signals. If you push trades to a different PickMyTrade account, also check its token.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q11_q: Which assets and brokers on TradeLocker are supported?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q11_a: PickMyTrade works with whatever instruments your TradeLocker broker offers, which usually means forex pairs (for example EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY), CFDs, indices, commodities, and metals. Because TradeLocker is white-labelled by many brokers, your exact symbols, spreads, and hours come from your specific broker, and PickMyTrade routes the orders your alerts create to that account.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q12_q: Does this work with prop firms that use TradeLocker, and what are the rules?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q12_a: PickMyTrade can connect to a TradeLocker account whether it is personal, demo, or funded, and some prop firms do run on TradeLocker. Copy trading and automation rules vary by prop firm and change over time, so always confirm your firm's current policy before you automate. Firms differ on whether they allow webhook automation, how many accounts you may copy across, and how identical fills can be. PickMyTrade copies your own alerts across your own accounts, but staying inside each firm's rules is your responsibility.
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q13_q: How much does it cost and is there a free trial?
broker_tradelocker.new_faq_q13_a: PickMyTrade is $50 per month or $500 per year, and every plan starts with a 7-day free trial with no credit card required. One subscription covers both single-account automation and the multi-account trade copier, plus 24/7 live support.

broker_tradestation.tsfaq_a8: Buy Alert: Opens or adds to a long position; closes any open short position first. Sell Alert: Opens or adds to a short position; closes any open long position first. Close Alert: Closes all open positions and cancels pending orders.

best_trade_copier.pricing_compared_title: Trade copier pricing compared: flat vs per-account vs per-connection vs one-time
best_trade_copier.pricing_compared_p1: Trade copier pricing falls into four shapes, and the right one depends on how many accounts you run. Flat pricing charges one price no matter how many accounts sit under a login, so it gets cheaper per account as you scale; PickMyTrade at 50 dollars a month for unlimited accounts under one login, TradeDupe's flat tiers and PropSyncX near 44.99 dollars a month are examples. Per-connection or per-account tiers, like TradeSyncer's roughly 49 to 149 dollars a month by connection count, are fine for a couple of accounts but climb once you pass three or four.
best_trade_copier.pricing_compared_p2: Account-count caps by plan, as Copygram uses from around 25 dollars a month, keep the entry cheap but can force an upgrade as you add accounts. One-time or lifetime licenses, like Copilink's roughly 128 dollars lifetime, are the cheapest over years but are usually local software you host and maintain yourself. So the honest rule of thumb is simple: if you run many accounts, flat pricing almost always wins; if you run one or two local NinjaTrader accounts forever, a one-time license can be cheaper.

best_trade_copier.propfirm_rules_title: Prop-firm rules to check before you copy
best_trade_copier.propfirm_rules_p1: This is where most copier guides go quiet, so here is the honest part. PickMyTrade connects to accounts on Tradovate, Rithmic and ProjectX, which many prop firms run on, including names such as Apex, Topstep, Alpha Futures, Take Profit Trader, FundedNext Futures, MyFundedFutures, TradeDay and Tradeify. Copy trading and automation rules vary by prop firm and change over time, so always confirm your firm's current policy. We do not call any firm copy-trading friendly, because that can change with a single policy update.
best_trade_copier.propfirm_rules_p2: Four rules are worth checking on your firm's site before you connect a copier. First, consistency rules, which can limit how much of your profit comes from one day or one account. Second, any human-in-the-loop or semi-automated requirement, since some firms want you present rather than fully hands-off. Third, account-count limits, meaning how many funded accounts you may copy across at once. Fourth, allowed platforms, since a firm may permit Tradovate but not another route.
best_trade_copier.propfirm_rules_p3: The safe framing that most firms share is the difference between internal copying, routing your own signals across your own funded accounts, and external copy trading, subscribing to a signal seller or letting someone manage your account. best_trade_copier.glossary1_def: The source account. Trades placed here, or signals routed to it, are what the copier replicates outward to other accounts.
best_trade_copier.glossary2_def: A destination account that receives copied trades, often sized by its own multiplier so it stays inside its own risk limit.
best_trade_copier.glossary3_def: The part of the copier that turns one source event into matching orders on every connected account, applying each account's size and rules.
best_trade_copier.glossary4_def: The delay between the source event and the order reaching your broker. It comes from the copier, the network, the broker and, for webhook tools, how fast the alert is sent.
best_trade_copier.glossary5_def: The difference between the expected price and the filled price. Faster copying reduces it, but volatility and liquidity matter more than raw copier speed.
best_trade_copier.glossary6_def: Settings or workflows, such as semi-automated or human-in-the-loop confirmation, that help you stay inside a prop firm's rules while copying.
best_trade_copier.faq_subtitle: Straight answers to the questions traders ask before choosing a copier.
best_trade_copier.faq_q1: What is the best trade copier for prop firms in 2026?
best_trade_copier.faq_a1: There is no single best copier; it depends on your platform and your firm. For TradingView-driven automation across Tradovate, Rithmic and ProjectX accounts on flat pricing, PickMyTrade fits that use case. For Tradovate-only prop stacks with rogue-trade controls, TradeDupe is strong. For NinjaTrader-based prop trading, Copilink or Tradecopia fit better. Whatever you choose, copy-trading and automation rules vary by prop firm and change over time, so confirm your firm's current policy first.
best_trade_copier.faq_q2: What is the best trade copier for Tradovate?
best_trade_copier.faq_a2: For copying one TradingView alert or one manual trade across unlimited Tradovate accounts under a single login on flat pricing, PickMyTrade fits that use case, and it also connects nine other brokers. TradeDupe is a Tradovate-only option with automatic rogue-trade closure, and Copygram focuses on Telegram and TradingView signals into Tradovate. Match the tool to where your signals come from.
best_trade_copier.faq_q3: What is the best trade copier for TradingView?
best_trade_copier.faq_a3: If your signals live in TradingView you want a copier that takes a webhook alert natively. PickMyTrade, TradeSyncer, Tradecopia and PropSyncX all accept TradingView webhooks. PickMyTrade is cloud-based with no VPS, connects ten brokers, and copies to unlimited accounts under one login for a flat 50 dollars a month. Webhook alerts need a paid TradingView plan (Pro, Pro+ or Premium).
best_trade_copier.faq_q4: What is the fastest trade copier, and does latency actually matter for my strategy?
best_trade_copier.faq_a4: Local and desktop copiers, and some websocket cloud routes, advertise the lowest numbers, from single-digit milliseconds to under 100ms, but most of those figures are vendor self-reported and not independently tested. PickMyTrade processes your order in under 200ms on our side; total fill time also depends on your broker, network latency and how quickly TradingView sends the alert. For swing and most intraday strategies the difference rarely changes your result. For sub-second scalping, a local copier sitting next to your platform may edge out any cloud tool.
best_trade_copier.faq_q5: How much do trade copiers cost, and is flat pricing cheaper than per-account pricing when I scale accounts?
best_trade_copier.faq_a5: Expect roughly 25 to 150 dollars a month, plus a few one-time or lifetime licenses. Flat pricing, like PickMyTrade at 50 dollars a month for unlimited accounts under one login, gets cheaper per account the more accounts you run. Per-connection or per-account tiers can climb quickly once you pass three or four accounts. A one-time license is cheapest over the long run but is usually local software you host and maintain yourself.
best_trade_copier.faq_q6: Which trade copiers are cloud-based (no VPS) vs local (NinjaTrader/desktop)?
best_trade_copier.faq_a6: Cloud with no VPS: PickMyTrade, TradeSyncer, PropSyncX, Lune and Copygram. Local or desktop: Copilink, which is a NinjaTrader 8 add-on, and Tradecopia's desktop application. Cloud copiers keep running when your computer is off; local copiers can be lower latency but need your machine or a VPS to stay online.
best_trade_copier.faq_q7: Do prop firms allow trade copying, and which rules (consistency, semi-auto) do I need to follow?
best_trade_copier.faq_a7: Many futures prop firms run on Tradovate, Rithmic or ProjectX and let you copy your own signals across your own funded accounts, but the rules vary by firm and change over time. Common ones to check are consistency rules, a human-in-the-loop or semi-automated requirement, limits on how many accounts you can copy across, and which platforms are allowed. Always confirm your firm's current policy before you go live, and never assume a firm is copy-trading friendly.
best_trade_copier.faq_q8: Is there a free trade copier, or a free trial?
best_trade_copier.faq_a8: Genuinely free-forever copiers are rare and usually trade off on reliability, support or account limits. The honest middle ground is a free trial. PickMyTrade offers a 7-day free trial with no credit card required, and several rivals offer 7-day trials. Copilink also sells a low-cost one-time lifetime license if you would rather avoid a subscription.
best_trade_copier.faq_q9: What is the difference between a TradingView-to-broker copier and account-to-account mirroring?
best_trade_copier.faq_a9: A TradingView-to-broker copier starts from a signal: your alert fires and the tool places that trade on every connected account. Account-to-account mirroring starts from a fill: you trade on a leader account and the tool mirrors that fill to follower accounts. PickMyTrade does both, a TradingView webhook copier and a manual master-to-followers copier. Pure mirroring tools like TradeDupe and Tradecopia focus on the leader-follower model.
best_trade_copier.faq_q10: Which trade copier works across multiple brokers and multiple funded accounts at once?
best_trade_copier.faq_a10: PickMyTrade copies across ten brokers including Tradovate, Rithmic, Interactive Brokers, TradeStation, TradeLocker, ProjectX, Match-Trader, Tradier, cTrader and Ironbeam, and mirrors one signal to unlimited accounts under a single login. Lune, TradeSyncer and PropSyncX also do cross-broker copying across futures platforms. If all your accounts sit under one Tradovate login, a Tradovate-native tool can be enough.

broker_faq_detail.funding_q4: How long do deposits take to reflect in my {name} account?
broker_faq_detail.funding_a4: Bank wires may take 1-3 business days. ACH transfers may take 2-5 business days. Check {name}'s current funding FAQ for up-to-date timelines.
broker_faq_detail.funding_a5: Regulated brokers follow client money segregation rules set by their regulator. Verify {name}'s regulatory status and check whether client funds are segregated or covered by any compensation scheme before depositing. PickMyTrade never holds your funds.
broker_faq_detail.funding_q6: Can someone with my {name} API keys withdraw my money?
broker_faq_detail.funding_a6: API keys with trading-only permissions cannot initiate withdrawals on most platforms. broker_faq_detail.security_a1: Regulation depends on your jurisdiction. Verify {name}'s current regulatory status with the relevant authority (CFTC/NFA, FCA, ASIC, etc.) before opening an account. Regulations and registrations change — always check official regulator websites.
broker_faq_detail.security_a2: Yes, {name} supports 2FA via an authenticator app (TOTP) and/or SMS. Always enable 2FA on your account and on your email address. Use an authenticator app rather than SMS where possible for better security.
broker_faq_detail.security_q3: Is it safe to give my {name} API keys to PickMyTrade?
broker_faq_detail.security_a3: PickMyTrade stores API credentials encrypted and uses them only to submit orders under your direction. Best practice: generate keys with trading-only permissions (no withdrawal), set IP restrictions to PickMyTrade's servers, and rotate keys periodically.
broker_faq_detail.security_q4: What happens to my open positions if {name} goes down?
broker_faq_detail.security_a4: Exchange-side positions typically remain open even if the platform is temporarily unavailable. For futures and derivatives, positions stay with the clearinghouse. If {name}'s systems are down, contact their support to manage open positions manually.
broker_faq_detail.security_q5: Does {name} use cold storage for customer assets?
broker_faq_detail.security_a5: Most reputable exchanges hold the majority of customer assets in cold (offline) storage. Check {name}'s current security page for their exact custody and cold storage percentages.
broker_faq_detail.security_q6: What should I do if my {name} account is compromised?
broker_faq_detail.security_a6: Immediately freeze or cancel your API keys, change your account password, enable or re-enable 2FA, and contact {name} support. Also revoke PickMyTrade's connection and reconnect with new credentials once your account is secured.
broker_faq_detail.propfirm_a1: Several prop firms support {name} as a trading infrastructure provider. Check each prop firm's platform page to confirm whether they currently offer {name} credentials, as partnerships change frequently.
broker_faq_detail.propfirm_q2: Can I automate a prop firm {name} account with PickMyTrade?
broker_faq_detail.propfirm_a2: Yes — prop accounts accessed via {name} plug into PickMyTrade like any standard connection. Always confirm the prop firm's current rules on automated trading and copy trading before running strategies on a live account.
broker_faq_detail.propfirm_q3: Will a prop firm ban me for running an automated strategy through {name}?
broker_faq_detail.propfirm_a3: Most prop firms allow automation, but each firm has its own rules on consistency, max drawdown, news trading, and copy trading. Read the current rulebook carefully — violations in automated mode can void payouts even if the trades were profitable.
broker_faq_detail.propfirm_q4: Does my prop firm eval login work after I get funded?
broker_faq_detail.propfirm_a4: Typically you receive new credentials for the funded (PA) account — the eval login does not automatically roll over. Update your PickMyTrade connection with the new credentials when you transition to a funded account.

broker_faq_detail.propfirm_a5: Yes. PickMyTrade treats each {name} login as a separate connection, so you can route one TradingView alert to multiple prop firm accounts simultaneously.
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_q1: My {name} API key is not working — what should I check?
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_a1: Common causes: (1) Key does not have trading permissions enabled, (2) IP restriction set to a different IP than PickMyTrade's servers, (3) Key was generated on a different account or sub-account, (4) Key was regenerated and the old one is now invalid. broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_q2: Orders are not executing — what could be wrong?
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_a2: Check: (1) TradingView alert message JSON is valid and matches PickMyTrade's expected format, (2) Webhook URL is correctly pasted in TradingView, (3) {name} API keys are active and have trading permissions, (4) Market is open, (5) Account has sufficient balance/margin.
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_q3: Why is my {name} connection showing as disconnected in PickMyTrade?
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_a3: API keys may have expired, been regenerated, or had permissions revoked. Re-enter your {name} API credentials in PickMyTrade. Also check if {name} has any ongoing outages on their status page.
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_q4: Why am I getting "insufficient margin" errors?
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_a4: Your account does not have enough free margin to open the position at the specified size. Reduce the quantity in your PickMyTrade strategy settings, deposit more funds, or close existing positions to free margin before retrying.
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_q5: My alert fired but no order was placed — how do I debug this?
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_a5: Check the PickMyTrade activity log for the alert — it will show whether the alert was received, what order was attempted, and any rejection message from {name}. Common causes: invalid symbol format, market closed, or insufficient funds.
broker_faq_detail.troubleshooting_a6: For {name}-specific issues (account, funds, API access), contact {name}'s support team directly via their Help Center or live chat. For PickMyTrade automation issues, contact PickMyTrade support at pickmytrade.io or via the in-app chat.

propfirm_faq_detail.basics_a1: {name} is a proprietary trading firm that provides funded accounts to traders who pass an evaluation. You pay an evaluation fee, reach a profit target without breaking the drawdown rules, and move to a funded account where you keep a share of the profits. The Key facts table above lists {name}'s current plans and payout terms.
propfirm_faq_detail.basics_a2: Always verify independently before purchasing. Check the firm's official documentation. Read the funded trader agreement carefully before paying any evaluation fee. Prop firm rules, fees, and payout policies change frequently.
propfirm_faq_detail.basics_q3: Are {name} accounts real money or simulated?
propfirm_faq_detail.basics_a3: Retail prop firm accounts, including those at {name}, typically run on simulated infrastructure that mirrors real market data. Payouts are funded from the firm's evaluation revenue rather than from live market profits. The Key facts table above shows how {name}'s funded accounts are structured.
propfirm_faq_detail.basics_a4: Prop firms generally operate as technology or contractor companies rather than regulated broker-dealers or FCMs, so they are typically not registered with the SEC, CFTC, FINRA, or FCA. The relationship is governed by the trader agreement, not by securities regulation. Read {name}'s agreement for its exact legal terms before paying.
propfirm_faq_detail.accounttypes_a1: {name} offers evaluation programs in which you reach a profit target while staying inside drawdown limits. Each model differs in account size, target, and drawdown type. The Key facts table above shows which models {name} offers right now.
propfirm_faq_detail.accounttypes_q2: What is the difference between the evaluation and funded account at {name}?
propfirm_faq_detail.accounttypes_a2: The evaluation is the test phase where you must hit a profit target without breaching drawdown rules. The funded account is the phase you graduate into after passing, where you can request payouts based on your trading performance. Rules, drawdown types, and payout mechanics often differ between the two phases.
propfirm_faq_detail.accounttypes_a3: Some prop firms sell instant funding alongside standard evaluations: you skip the profit-target phase, usually pay more, and often get stricter drawdown or payout terms. Whether {name} offers it is covered in the Key facts table above.
propfirm_faq_detail.accounttypes_q4: Can I run multiple funded accounts at {name}?
propfirm_faq_detail.accounttypes_a4: Running several funded accounts at once is common, often with a per-person cap. Firms usually restrict hedging between accounts and copying trades across them in ways that look like one position split up. The Key facts table above shows the account limit for {name}.
propfirm_faq_detail.pricing_a1: Prop firms sell evaluations in several account sizes, from small starter accounts to large ones, and the fee rises with size. Promotional discounts can change the price a lot. See the Key facts table above for {name}'s sizes and fees and the date they were checked.
propfirm_faq_detail.pricing_q2: Does {name} charge monthly fees or one-time fees?
propfirm_faq_detail.pricing_a2: Evaluation pricing follows one of two models: a recurring monthly subscription until you pass, or a one-time fee per attempt. The model affects total cost if you need several attempts. The Key facts table above states which one {name} uses.
propfirm_faq_detail.pricing_a3: Prop firms often run recurring promotions around holidays and product launches, usually through promo codes or newsletters. Codes change quickly, so a code from an aggregator may already be expired. Compare {name}'s discounted price with the standard fee in the Key facts table above.
propfirm_faq_detail.targets_q1: What are the profit targets on {name} evaluations?
propfirm_faq_detail.targets_a1: The profit target is the amount you must earn in an evaluation to pass, set as a percentage of the starting balance (commonly 6-10%). A bigger account means a bigger dollar target. {name}'s targets per plan are in the Key facts table above.
propfirm_faq_detail.targets_q2: Do profit targets exist on funded accounts at {name}?
propfirm_faq_detail.targets_a2: Many prop firms drop the profit target once you are funded and focus on drawdown limits and payout eligibility, such as minimum profit and number of winning days. So the goal shifts from hitting a target to staying consistent. {name}'s funded-phase terms are summarised above.
propfirm_faq_detail.targets_q3: Does {name} evaluate on closing balance or floating equity?
propfirm_faq_detail.targets_a3: Profit targets are usually measured on closed (realized) P&L, not floating equity, so you must close positions for gains to count toward the target. An open winning trade alone will not pass the evaluation. Confirm {name}'s measurement basis in the Key facts table above.
propfirm_faq_detail.drawdown_q1: What type of drawdown does {name} use?
propfirm_faq_detail.drawdown_a1: A drawdown limit caps how much you can lose. The main types are trailing drawdown (the floor rises with your profits), static maximum drawdown (a fixed floor from the starting balance), and a daily loss limit. See the Key facts table above for {name}'s type and amounts.
propfirm_faq_detail.drawdown_q2: Does the drawdown at {name} apply to unrealized (floating) P&L?
propfirm_faq_detail.drawdown_a2: Drawdown is measured either on equity (including open positions) or on balance (closed trades only). Intraday trailing drawdowns follow unrealized P&L tick by tick, while end-of-day drawdowns update only at session close. Which basis {name} uses is shown in the Key facts table above.
propfirm_faq_detail.drawdown_q3: What happens when I breach the drawdown at {name}?
propfirm_faq_detail.drawdown_a3: Breaching the drawdown limit normally liquidates open positions and closes the account. In an evaluation you must buy a new one or pay for a reset, if the firm offers resets. The Key facts table above notes {name}'s breach consequences.
propfirm_faq_detail.drawdown_q4: What is a daily loss limit (DLL) at {name}?
propfirm_faq_detail.drawdown_a4: A daily loss limit (DLL) caps your loss within one trading day. Breaching it usually suspends trading until the next session instead of closing the account, though some firms treat it as a full breach. {name}'s DLL amounts are in the Key facts table above.
propfirm_faq_detail.consistency_a1: Many prop firms enforce a consistency rule that limits how much of your total profit can come from a single trading day — typically expressed as a maximum percentage (e.g., 30–50%). This prevents traders from qualifying via one large lucky trade. Check whether {name} enforces this rule and the exact threshold.
propfirm_faq_detail.consistency_q2: Does violating the consistency rule fail my account at {name}?
propfirm_faq_detail.consistency_a2: Typically, violating the consistency rule blocks a payout request rather than failing the account. You would need to trade additional smaller-profit days to bring your best-day percentage back under the threshold before requesting a payout. Confirm {name}'s exact policy.
propfirm_faq_detail.consistency_q3: Does the consistency rule reset after a payout at {name}?
propfirm_faq_detail.consistency_a3: The consistency clock usually resets after each approved payout, so the next payout cycle starts from zero and earlier big days no longer count against you. Whether this applies to {name} is stated in the Key facts table above.

futures_trade_copier.s2_h2: What a futures trade copier does
futures_trade_copier.s2_p1: A futures trade copier takes one source trade and mirrors it across several futures accounts at the same time. You choose a leader account, sometimes called the master, and every follower account receives the same entry, exit, stop-loss and take-profit automatically. Instead of placing the same order by hand on account after account, you set the copier up once and it does the repeating for you. That is the heart of futures copy trading: one decision, many accounts, no missed fills while you switch windows.
futures_trade_copier.s2_p2: The part that makes a copy trader for futures genuinely useful is the ratio. Every follower account gets its own position-size multiplier, so the copier is not forced to trade the same contract count everywhere. You can run a small evaluation at 0.5x, a mid-size funded account at 1x and a larger account at 2x, all from the same source signal, so each account stays inside its own risk limit. This one-to-many model with per-account sizing is exactly what prop-firm traders reach for when they scale from one account to a dozen.
futures_trade_copier.s2_p3: PickMyTrade is a futures copy trader built around that model, with two ways to feed it. The rest of this page covers both paths, the brokers and prop firms it copies between, how cross-broker copying and risk controls work, the real setup steps, an honest comparison with other futures trade copier software, and the questions traders ask most.
futures_trade_copier.s3_subtitle: Two distinct copy modes cover both automated and discretionary traders. Use whichever fits how you trade, or use both.

futures_trade_copier.s3_card1_desc: One TradingView alert, indicator or Pine Script signal fires and PickMyTrade executes the matching futures order across every connected account at once. All entries, exits, stop-loss and take-profit copy from the source with the same prices on each account. This path carries the full feature set: five stop-loss and take-profit methods, trailing stop, reverse or flip position, and scale-in.
futures_trade_copier.s3_card2_desc: Prefer to trade by hand? Place a trade on your master (admin) account and the Manual Trade Copier mirrors it out to your follower (sub) accounts in real time. Follower accounts under the same broker login are covered by one subscription, and every copied trade is tracked with a master and slave order ID, with a stop button to halt copying instantly. The Manual Trade Copier is currently Tradovate-specific.
futures_trade_copier.s3_cloud_p1: PickMyTrade runs entirely in the cloud, 24/7. There is no desktop app to babysit, no NinjaTrader DLL to install and no VPS bill. That is a real difference from older download-and-run futures copiers, which need a machine or a rented VPS switched on around the clock or they stop copying the moment your computer sleeps. With PickMyTrade, once your accounts are connected and your alert is live, trades copy even when your machine is off.
futures_trade_copier.s3_cloud_p2: Most searchers looking for a futures trade copier want the signal path (a TradingView trade copier), so the setup steps below focus on that, with the master-to-follower Manual Trade Copier as the second option for discretionary traders.
futures_trade_copier.s4_p1: PickMyTrade copies futures trades across the platforms most active futures and prop-firm traders actually use. It connects to Tradovate, Rithmic, Interactive Brokers, TradeStation, ProjectX, TradeLocker and Tradier for futures, and it also automates forex on TradeLocker. Every connection uses the same TradingView webhook engine, so one strategy can drive orders wherever your accounts live.
futures_trade_copier.s4_p2: To be clear about scope: PickMyTrade does not support MetaTrader (MT4 or MT5), DXtrade or NinjaTrader as broker rails, and it is not a Telegram signal copier. If a tool page promises you those, it is not this one. Sticking to the platforms above is what keeps the copier fast and reliable for futures.

futures_trade_copier.s5_h2: Copy futures trades across prop firm accounts
futures_trade_copier.s5_p1: The biggest reason traders want a futures trade copier is prop firms. If you run several evaluations or funded accounts, copying one signal across all of them is how you scale without watching every account by hand.
futures_trade_copier.s5_p_firms: PickMyTrade supports copy trading across Apex, Topstep, Alpha Futures, Take Profit Trader, FundedNext Futures, MyFundedFutures, TradeDay and Tradeify, along with other Tradovate-powered firms. Because you connect your own funded and evaluation accounts, you stay in control of every account and every trade.
futures_trade_copier.s5_p1_rules: Here is the honest part most tool pages skip. Copy-trading rules vary by prop firm and change over time. Many futures firms treat internal copying, routing your own TradingView alerts across funded accounts you own, differently from external copy trading such as subscribing to a third-party signal seller or letting someone else manage your funded account. PickMyTrade is built for the first case: it copies your own alerts across your own accounts, so you stay in control. Always confirm your firm's current policy before you go live.
futures_trade_copier.s5_p2_rules: Firms also set their own per-account risk limits, position-sizing rules and consistency rules, and they cap how many accounts you can copy across. Those rules change over time (as of 2026, for example, some firms have allowed copying across a set number of accounts). PickMyTrade respects each account's own risk limits and never bypasses a firm's rules, but the responsibility to check your specific firm's current automation policy before you go live stays with you. futures_trade_copier.s6_h2: Cross-broker copying: one strategy, many broker rails
futures_trade_copier.s6_p1: Most copiers lock you to a single broker. A cross-broker futures trade copier does not. Because your accounts at Tradovate, Rithmic, Interactive Brokers, TradeStation, ProjectX, TradeLocker and Tradier all connect to one PickMyTrade account, a single TradingView strategy can drive orders on accounts held at different brokers. If one prop firm runs on Tradovate and another runs on Rithmic or ProjectX, the same strategy still reaches both, so you standardize one system across whatever platform each account happens to use.
futures_trade_copier.s6_p2: This matters because prop firms and personal accounts rarely all sit on the same broker rail. Rather than run three separate tools, you connect every account once and let one signal fan out. It is genuine cross-broker automation driven from your strategy, not a workaround.
futures_trade_copier.s6_p3: One honest note on how it works: cross-broker copying here is signal-driven. One TradingView alert routes to your connected accounts across brokers. The master-to-follower Manual Trade Copier, where a fill on a master account mirrors to follower accounts, is currently Tradovate-specific, so we do not claim a fill on one broker automatically mirrors to a different broker. If your accounts span brokers, the TradingView path is how you copy across all of them.
futures_trade_copier.s7_p1: A copier is only as safe as its sizing. Every follower account in PickMyTrade gets its own quantity multiplier, and the math is simple: client position equals master position times the multiplier. So a 2-contract signal becomes 1 contract on a 0.5x account, 2 on a 1x account, 4 on a 2x account and 6 on a 3x account. Decimal multipliers like 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 are supported, and the final quantity rounds to a whole number. That lets a small evaluation, a mid-size funded account and a larger account all follow the same signal while each stays inside its own drawdown limit.
futures_trade_copier.s7_p2: Beyond the ratio, position size can be a fixed quantity or a risk percentage, so the copier fits both aggressive scaling and risk-first sizing. On the webhook path you can attach stop-loss and take-profit using five methods (points or dollar value, percentage, price levels, ticks, or total profit and loss), add a trailing stop, reverse or flip a position, or scale into an existing one, all from your alert. Reverse here means flipping a position (close the current one and open the opposite); PickMyTrade does not offer per-follower inverse copying, so we do not claim it.
futures_trade_copier.s7_note: Order-type note: the webhook path supports Market, Limit and Stop orders with the full risk toolkit above. The Manual Trade Copier supports Market, Limit, Stop, Stop-Limit and bracket orders on market entries, and does not include trailing stop or break-even.
futures_trade_copier.s8_p1: PickMyTrade processes your order in under 200ms on our side. When one signal fans out to many accounts, all connected accounts receive the trade within seconds. Your total fill time also depends on your broker, prop firm, network conditions and how quickly TradingView sends the alert, exactly as it does with any copier, so we state the number we can stand behind rather than a guaranteed end-to-end figure.
futures_trade_copier.s8_p2: You will see some futures copiers advertise colocated, single-digit-millisecond fills to the exchange. PickMyTrade does not compete in a colo latency race and does not claim numbers it has not measured. For the vast majority of TradingView and prop-firm strategies, under 200ms order processing on our side is fast enough that fill quality is driven by the market, not the copier. Where PickMyTrade wins is breadth and dependability: many brokers, cloud running with no VPS to crash, and a flat price.
futures_trade_copier.s8_p3: Reliability also comes from the cloud model itself. There is no local app that can freeze, no VPS session that can drop, and no need to leave a machine on. That is often the difference between a copier that quietly stops overnight and one that keeps working while you sleep.

You pick a leader (master) signal, and every follower account receives the same entry, exit, stop-loss and take-profit automatically, sized by a per-account ratio. With PickMyTrade the source can be a TradingView alert or a trade you place by hand on a master account, and the copies run in the cloud without you clicking through each account.

That is real cross-broker automation from one strategy. futures_trade_copier.s13_q6: Can I copy trades from a TradingView strategy or Pine Script to multiple futures accounts?

When your TradingView strategy, indicator or Pine Script alert fires, TradingView sends a webhook to PickMyTrade, which places the matching futures order on every connected account at once. futures_trade_copier.s13_q7: How do I copy trades across multiple prop firm accounts without breaking their rules?
futures_trade_copier.s13_a7: Copy-trading and automation rules vary by prop firm and change over time. Many futures firms treat internal copying, routing your own TradingView alerts across funded accounts you own, differently from external copy trading such as subscribing to a third-party signal seller or letting someone manage your account. PickMyTrade is built for the internal case: it copies your own alerts across your own accounts, respects each account's own risk limits and position sizing, and never bypasses a firm's rules. futures_trade_copier.s13_a8: PickMyTrade processes your order in under 200ms on our side. When one signal fans out to many accounts, all connected accounts receive the trade within seconds. cloud_trade_copier.s2_h2: What is a cloud trade copier?
cloud_trade_copier.s2_p1: A cloud trade copier copies one source trade across several accounts from remote servers, instead of from software running on your own computer. You connect your accounts once, and every entry, exit, stop-loss and take-profit copies automatically. Because the copier lives in the cloud, there is nothing to install, nothing to keep patched and nothing that stops working the moment you close your laptop. That is the whole idea: your trades copy whether you are at your desk, on your phone or asleep.
cloud_trade_copier.s2_p2: This is the opposite of the old download-and-run model. A traditional desktop copier installs on one machine, has to stay open, and usually needs a rented VPS so it keeps running when your home PC is off. cloud_trade_copier.s4_h2: Why no VPS is needed, and what that saves you
cloud_trade_copier.s4_p1: A VPS, or virtual private server, is a rented always-on computer in a data center. Traders use one so a desktop copier keeps running after they close their laptop. It solves a real problem, but it adds a real cost and a real chore: a monthly bill, an operating system to update, and one more thing that can crash at 3am while you are not watching. A no VPS trade copier removes that whole layer.
cloud_trade_copier.s4_p2: Because PickMyTrade already runs on managed cloud infrastructure, the always-on job is done for you. That means three concrete savings. First, cost: you pay one flat $50 per month for the copier and nothing for a server, instead of stacking a VPS rental on top of a copier license. Second, maintenance: there is no machine to patch, no app to reinstall after an update, and no plugin to reconnect. Third, single-machine risk: your copying does not depend on one PC or one VPS staying online, so a reboot, a Windows update or a power cut at home does not knock your trades offline.

cloud_trade_copier.s6_h2: When a local copier still wins, and why cloud fits most traders
cloud_trade_copier.s6_p1: We are not going to pretend cloud beats everything. If your entire edge is speed, a local copier installed on a server co-located near the exchange can reach lower raw latency than any cloud service, PickMyTrade included. A hardcore scalper firing dozens of tickets a session, chasing single-digit-millisecond fills, has a genuine reason to run local execution close to the matching engine. That is the one place where the old desktop model still has the edge, and some tools lean hard on this angle to pull scalpers toward a local setup.
cloud_trade_copier.s6_p2: For almost everyone else, that trade-off runs the other way. Swing traders, intraday traders, prop-account traders and anyone copying across multiple accounts are not competing on microseconds. What actually costs them money is a copier that goes down because a home PC rebooted, a VPS bill that eats into profit, or being unable to check positions because the tool is stuck on one machine. Cloud removes all three, and you still get order processing in under 200ms on our side.
cloud_trade_copier.s6_p3: So the honest rule of thumb is simple. If you need co-located, ultra-low-latency execution and you trade one platform, a local copier may suit you better. If you value reliability, zero install, the freedom to manage from any device, and reaching many accounts across 10 brokers without a plugin, a cloud trade copier is the better tool. Most traders sit firmly in the second group.
cloud_trade_copier.s7_p1: It is easy to find copier pages that promise a hard end-to-end fill speed. We will not, because no cloud service can honestly guarantee it. Here is what is true and measurable: PickMyTrade processes your order in under 200ms on our side. When one signal fans out to several accounts, they receive the trade within seconds.
cloud_trade_copier.s7_p2: Your total fill time also depends on things outside any copier's control: your broker's execution speed, network latency between the systems involved, and how quickly TradingView sends the alert in the first place. Those add up differently for every trader, which is exactly why a guaranteed end-to-end number would be marketing, not fact. What we can commit to is fast, consistent processing on our side and a fan-out that reaches every connected account quickly.
cloud_trade_copier.s7_p3: Reliability is where cloud quietly pulls ahead. Because there is no desktop app to crash and no single VPS to fall over, your copying does not hinge on one machine staying up. PickMyTrade runs 24/7 in the cloud, so once your accounts are connected and your alert is live, trades keep copying even when your computer is asleep or switched off. For high-frequency needs, review whether cloud latency fits your strategy before you commit; for most futures and multi-account traders, it does.

ai_ml_trading_plan.hero_answer_title: Quick answer: how do I use AI/ML for trading?
ai_ml_trading_plan.hero_answer_p1: You don't ask AI to predict prices. Instead, you keep a simple rule-based strategy (for example, a TradingView strategy) and train a machine-learning model to grade each trade idea — estimating the odds it hits its profit target before its stop-loss — so you only take the strongest setups.
ai_ml_trading_plan.hero_answer_p2: A second AI layer detects whether the market is calm or stormy and stands aside in storms, while fixed math rules (volatility targeting and fractional Kelly) decide position size. Execution is automated: your TradingView alert fires a webhook to PickMyTrade, which places the order — with take-profit and stop-loss brackets — at your connected broker. An AI copilot like Claude Fable can write all the Python code for you, so you don't need to be a programmer to start.
